description: Verified agronomic knowledge base for offline disease checking

symptoms: Brown to black spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Lower leaves turning yellow around spots and dropping prematurely
recommendations: Prune and safely destroy heavily infected lower leaves
Water at the base of the plant using drip irrigation; keep leaves dry
Ensure adequate spacing between plants for good airflow
Apply copper-based or approved mancozeb fungicide early in the morning
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops for 2 to 3 years
Mulch around the base of plants to prevent soil splash onto foliage
Use certified disease-free seeds and seedlings
organic_management: Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) as an early preventative
Apply Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens to soil and foliage
Spray diluted sour buttermilk (1:10 with water) on foliage
Tomato.regional_advice: Common in warm, humid weather and during monsoon transitions in South & Central India.
Tomato.farmer_message: Act early when you see concentric spots on lower leaves to prevent spread to developing fruits.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown or purplish lesions on leaves and stems
White fungal fuzz visible on the underside of leaves in cool, moist mornings
Rapid wilting and collapse of leaves
recommendations: Immediately destroy severely affected plants to protect the remaining field
Apply systemic fungicide recommended by your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra immediately
prevention: Monitor plants closely during foggy, cool, overcast periods
organic_management: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) as a protective spray before persistent rains
Neem oil foliar spray (3-5 ml per liter of water)
Tomato.regional_advice: Highly destructive during cloudy, cool winter mornings in hilly and plateau regions.
Tomato.farmer_message: Late blight spreads rapidly in cool moist weather. Immediate field sanitation is essential.

symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and thickening of leaves
Severe stunting and bushy appearance of the plant
Flowers dropping off without setting fruit
recommendations: Rogue out and bury infected plants immediately to reduce virus reservoir
Install yellow sticky traps (10-12 traps per acre)
prevention: Grow barrier crops like maize or sorghum (3-4 border rows)
Use whitefly-proof nylon nets in nursery beds
organic_management: Spray neem oil (5 ml/L) mixed with mild soap emulsifier to deter whiteflies
Spray Agniastra or Dashaparni ark weekly during vector peak season
Tomato.regional_advice: Whitefly vectors peak in dry, hot months before the rains.
Tomato.farmer_message: The virus is spread by whiteflies. Controlling the pest early protects the whole crop.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves without spots, lesions, or wilting
recommendations: Maintain balanced nutrition with well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM)
Ensure uniform soil moisture; avoid water stress during flowering
Inspect leaf undersides weekly for early pest signs
prevention: Maintain field sanitation and remove weeds from bunds
organic_management: Apply Jeevamrutha or Panchagavya every 15 days to enhance natural vigor
Tomato.regional_advice: Continue standard agronomic practices for your region.
Tomato.farmer_message: Your crop appears healthy! Keep up regular monitoring and soil health management.
